messages:
jordan: heads-up — customer ACME is seeing ~500 JSON-mode parse failures since 03:00 UTC, user flow broken. logs show invalid JSON when client tries to parse responses. :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: ALERT: structured-output-parse-rate > 5% for deployment redwood-prod-us-east (alert id: svc-9012)

sophia: @jordan can you paste a sample request_id and the raw model output (redacted as needed)? need something reproducible. :eyes:

jordan: request-id: abc-123-req. sample below (we redacted PII but left structure):
```
PROMPT: extract_contacts from email thread
MODE: json
EXPECTED_SCHEMA: [{"name":"string","email":"string","role":"string"}]
MODEL_OUTPUT:
{"results": [{"name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@***.com", "role": "PM"}, {"name": "Bob Smith", "email": "bob@***.com", "role": "Eng"}] } extra commentary: see follow-up
```

sophia: that trailing ` extra commentary` would break strict JSON parsing. did we start stripping/rewriting parts of the model output in the logging pipeline?

taylor: quick check — does the model actually return the extra text, or is it appended by our postproc/redaction step? can someone grab span traces for abc-123-req from the inference gateway and the logging microservice?

luis: I pulled the trace. In the gateway span the payload is valid JSON (no trailing commentary). After our redaction service the bytes look like:
```
{"results": [{"name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@★.com", "role": "PM"}, {"name": "Bob Smith", "email": "bob@★.com", "role": "Eng"}] ★}
```
so redaction replaced `@***.com` with `@★.com` AND added an extra star at the end — that final char breaks the parser. redaction bug confirmed.

sophia: wow — redaction should never mutate JSON structure. looks like our regex replace is not JSON-aware. tagging @eng-infra and @eng-runtime.

jordan: impact note: customer retried requests on client, causing increased token usage and billing spike. billing-team can you estimate delta?

billing-team: we see a 18% uptick in ACME invoice window 03:00-04:30 UTC, roughly $420 extra. recommend temporary mitigation: 1) disable auto-retries for JSON-mode in SDK for that customer; 2) enable fallback to `text` mode for extraction endpoints so client can still proceed; 3) we'll issue credit if confirmed caused by our redaction bug.

taylor: mitigation steps landed: feature-flagged fallback to text-mode and throttling rule applied to 10.0.3.0/24 for ACME. also created a short-term rule to route JSON-mode responses through the pre-redaction audit log (no redaction) to debug. we need to ensure PII isn't leaked — these logs are limited to SRE+support and will be auto-deleted after 7d.

sophia: longer-term: add metric `structured_output.parse_failures` (counter) + `parse_failure.reason` tag (e.g., trailing_bytes, malformed_value, missing_field, redaction_mutation). Also alert when rate > 1% for any customer for 15m.

luis: i'll open a PR to make redaction JSON-aware (parse tokens then mask strings instead of blind regex). will also add a redaction-audit span attribute that stores `redaction_applied=true|false` and `redaction_patch_hash=<sha256>` to correlate.

jordan: repro steps for eng-runtime:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: abc-123-req" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-open-0", "mode":"json", "prompt":"extract_contacts: ..."}'
# observe response bytes in gateway vs downstream logging service
```

sophia: i've updated the support runbook with: how to find pre/post-redaction traces, how to add the parse_status filter on the structured-output dashboard, and a snippet for customers to temporarily set `mode=text` in SDK. link to runbook pinned in #support-docs.

billing-team: we'll draft a credit note and hold final approval until infra confirms root cause.

taylor: action items: (1) luis fix redaction -> v1 patch by EOD; (2) sophia add metric + alert; (3) jordan coordinate customer comms + credit; (4) taylor keep fallback in place until patch deployed. tagging @oncall-bot to keep monitor on for 6h. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Monitor rule applied: watch structured_output.parse_failures for abc-123-req customer for next 6h. alerting on sustained >1%

sophia: thanks team. small follow-up — we should redact with placeholders that preserve JSON token lengths? or better: replace inner strings but keep JSON separators intact. i'll add a doc note. :memo:

jordan: closing note: customer patched client to not retry, confirmed flow back to green after fallback. keeping the thread open until redaction patch deploys. :+1:
